data.title: Diphenhydramine
data.body:
_More from Khopkar · Antihistamines_

**Class:** First-generation H1 antihistamine — ethanolamine

## Mechanism of action
- H1 inverse agonist; strongly sedative and anticholinergic; local anaesthetic effect

## Indications in dermatology & STI
- Acute allergic reactions, urticaria, night-time itch, anaphylaxis adjunct
- 1% injection as local anaesthetic in patients allergic to amides and esters

## Dose & formulations
- 25–50 mg every 4–6 h (max 300 mg/day); injection 10–50 mg IV/IM

## Adverse effects
- Marked sedation, impaired performance, anticholinergic delirium in elderly
- Topical diphenhydramine: frequent contact sensitiser and photosensitiser

## Contraindications
- Neonates, breastfeeding; caution in elderly (Beers list)

## Drug interactions
- CNS depressants; CYP2D6 inhibitor (raises metoprolol, TCAs)

## Pregnancy & lactation
Has been used; avoid near term.

## Viva points
- Can be used as an alternative local anaesthetic (1%) in 'caine' allergy
- Avoid topical antihistamines — sensitisation

_Sources: Khopkar (First generation H1 antihistamines); Wolverton 4e ch.32 and ch.58. Facts summarised in our own words; Wolverton followed where books differ._
